title: Portobello Heritage Trust, Edinburgh,high days and holidays
text:

These photographs of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, opening the refurbished playpark in Mount Lodge in, we 
believe, 1971 sparked much discussion on social media in Portobello. Why Prince Philip came to open the park is 
unknown, but as it probably took place at the end of June, the Royal family would be in residence at Holyrood 
Palace.
One striking aspect of the photograph is the lack of security surrounding the prince, an indicator of how much 
tighter security surrounding the Royal family has become in the past fifty years. We believe the man accompanying 
Prince Philip is Conservative Councillor Kenneth Borthwick who later became Lord Provost of Edinburgh.
The colours in these photographs do not seem to be particularly true. This can be noticed most in the colour of the 
men’s suits, which seem to be various shades of brown, and the boys’ school trousers. They would probably all be 
grey.
Children from Towerbank, St John’s and Brunstane primary schools were sent along to the playpark for the prince’s 
visit. They appear to be having a good time. The boat, named Blue Peter, was apparently set on fire in the early 
1970s. Do you recognise yourself in the photograph? If so, please get in touch at
admin@portobelloheritagetrust.co.uk
